name: Close-Grip Machine Chest Fly
summary: An isolation exercise performed seated on a fly machine using a narrow handle grip to target the pectoral muscles through horizontal adduction.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine handles align horizontally with mid-chest level.
Sit back firmly against the backrest with your feet planted flat on the floor.
Grasp the inner or narrow handle attachments with a neutral grip and maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
steps: Engage your chest and pull the handles together in a smooth arc until your hands nearly touch in front of your sternum.
Squeeze your pectoral muscles intensely at peak contraction for a brief pause.
Slowly reverse the movement under control, allowing your chest to open until you feel a comfortable stretch without letting the weight stack touch down.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you bring the handles together; inhale as you slowly return to the stretched starting position.
cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep your chest high and shoulders pinned back.
Squeeze the chest at the center.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the shoulders to shrug or roll forward at the end of the press.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the backrest throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Overextending the arms backward and hyperextending the shoulder capsule.
common_faults.correction: Stop the eccentric phase when your elbows are roughly in line with your torso, feeling tension in the chest rather than the shoulder joint.

common_faults.fault: Letting the weight plates crash between repetitions.
common_faults.correction: Maintain continuous muscular tension by stopping just short of the weight stack resting.

precautions: Do not set the starting arm range too far back if you have a history of anterior shoulder instability.
